alternatives.root_cause: A dependency of fraud-detection (Kafka or flagd) became slow and fraud-detection blocked waiting on it
alternatives.why_not: The ~1s spans are entirely self-time within fraud-detection's own process span with no child dependency span absorbing the time, and the delay is exactly 1.000s per record, which is a coded sleep rather than organic dependency latency

alternatives.root_cause: A configuration value controlling consumer behaviour was set wrong
alternatives.why_not: Change history for fraud-detection is empty over 24h, and the service attributes the delay to a runtime flag evaluation rather than a configuration file value

alternatives.root_cause: fraud-detection exhausted threads or connections and queued work backed up
alternatives.why_not: No exhaustion signals in the log, error ratio is flat or lower than baseline, and the stall duration is a uniform fixed interval rather than the degrading queue-growth pattern exhaustion produces

verdict.summary: A runtime feature flag ('kafkaQueueProblems') served by flagd was enabled, driving fraud-detection's order-consume path into a deliberate per-record 1-second sleep, so message processing stalled without any artifact or configuration change.
verdict.reasoning: The error-ratio metric for the alerting service showed no sustained departure from baseline (tr_51602c851bf6), so this is a latency/stall incident, not a failure incident. The service's own logs during the incident window repeatedly report a named feature flag being enabled and a one-second sleep per consumed record, with the same order id reprocessed over and over (tr_29b3ba9ec320). Traces corroborate this mechanically: many sibling spans of almost exactly ~1000ms self-time under a single root, with the degrading hop entirely self-time inside fraud-detection and no error flags (tr_0776b8650419). Change history for both fraud-detection and flagd is empty over a 24h window (tr_fb45e8957907, tr_8dc6bcd4d1a3), which is exactly the signature of a flag flipped in the flag store rather than a deploy or config edit. flagd appears in the blast radius only as the flag source; it is not itself failing, and no downstream dependency shows up in the self-time breakdown, which rules out dependency latency from an external service. Remediation is to revert the flag value in the flag store.
open_questions: Who flipped the kafkaQueueProblems flag and when it was flipped relative to the 21:47:31 onset, since the flag store carries no change record
Whether the flag was intentionally enabled for a test/game-day or flipped in error
Whether downstream order processing suffered data duplication from the repeated consumption of the same order id
